page: Microsoft Azure F2-1ams_v7 is an entry-level virtual machine within the compute-optimized Famsv7 series, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU sourced from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Despite its single vCPU configuration, it is provisioned with 16.0 GB of memory, resulting in a substantial 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring remote persistent disks for data retention.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong single-threaded compute efficiency balanced against lower aggregate throughput due to the single-core limitation. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server recorded 3,743.89 operations per second, placing it in the top tier (top 10%). It also scored in the top 10% for single-threaded gzip compression (38.98 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.88 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-core metrics mirror the single-core constraint, placing stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU overall scores in the bottom 25%. Memory benchmarks demonstrate mid-tier performance, achieving 42.75 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 32.15 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth.

From an architectural tradeoff perspective, the F2-1ams_v7 delivers high single-thread clock speeds and ample memory capacity for a single core, making it cost-efficient for memory-heavy single-threaded workloads. However, with only one core and bottom-tier multi-threaded, database, and web-serving results, it is poorly suited for concurrent throughput scenarios. Best-fit use cases include memory-intensive batch processing, single-threaded ETL pipelines, compression tasks, and lightweight utility services requiring significant memory headroom without multi-core overhead.
description: Microsoft Azure F2-1ams_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring a single dedicated vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of memory. It includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The instance contains no local storage or GPUs, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing reveals top-tier single-threaded performance, excelling in stress-ng single-core compute and gzip compression. However, overall multi-core compute, Redis SET operations, and web serving throughput fall into lower percentiles due to the single-core configuration. With an unusually high 16:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the F2-1ams_v7 is suited for single-threaded batch execution, memory-heavy data transformation, and lightweight background automation requiring dedicated memory headroom.
